links.actions: UN Group of Experts reported 3,000-4,000 Rwanda Defence Force troops operating in North Kivu alongside M23.
links.returns: Coltan from M23-held Rubaya traced into Rwandan supply chains.
links.position: Rwanda denies supporting M23 and cites the FDLR threat on its border.

links.actions: UN Panel found allegations of UAE arms deliveries to the RSF via eastern Chad credible. OFAC designated seven UAE-based companies that supplied the RSF with money and equipment.
links.returns: Sudanese gold bought by UAE-based AZ Gold and moved to Dubai. Account accessible to RSF procurement chief.
links.position: The UAE denies arming any party and says its flights carry humanitarian aid. The OFAC targets are private firms, not the UAE state.

links.actions: SWISSAID found 405 t of African gold imported into the UAE in 2022 was not declared as exports by African countries. 80-85% of African ASM gold went to the UAE.
links.returns: Gold refining and trade volume for Dubai. Undeclared value of about US$30.7bn for 2022 smuggling.
links.position: The UAE has said it is tightening due-diligence rules for gold refiners.

links.actions: Reuters (2021) reported the proposed Wagner deal at about $10.8m a month for ~1,000 fighters (terms not independently confirmed). Wagner left Mali in June 2025. The Kremlin-controlled Africa Corps stayed, about 70-80% ex-Wagner.
links.returns: Stake for Russia's Yadran Group in the Bamako gold refinery (see ru-mali-gold).
links.position: Bamako and Moscow describe it as state-to-state security cooperation.

links.actions: Construction of a 200 t/yr gold refinery began June 2025. Mali holds 62%, Yadran and a Swiss investor the rest.
links.returns: Minority stake in refining of Malian gold.
links.position: Mali presents it as ending raw-gold exports and asserting economic sovereignty.

links.actions: OFAC: Wagner-linked Midas holds rights to the Ndassima gold mine and with Wagner denied CAR inspectors access. Diamville converted CAR gold into dollars.
links.returns: Ndassima gold rights (deposit assessed >US$1bn) and CAR gold and diamond trade.
links.position: CAR's government describes Russian personnel as instructors invited under a bilateral agreement.

links.actions: Contract and end-user records show Baykar sent at least US$120m of weapons, including TB2 drones and hundreds of warheads, to the SAF in 2024.
links.returns: Not public in sources used (sale revenue only).
links.position: Baykar did not deny the sale in the cited report. Ankara backs the SAF-led government as Sudan's legitimate authority.

links.actions: Satellite imagery showed a Mohajer-6 at the SAF's Wadi Sayyidna base (Jan 2024). Six Qeshm Fars Air cargo flights went from Iran to Port Sudan in Dec 2023-Jan 2024.
links.returns: Not established. WSJ reported (Mar 2024) Iran sought a Red Sea base in return. Sudan and Iran both denied it. Diplomatic ties restored in 2023.
links.position: A senior SAF source denied the drones came directly from Iran.

links.actions: Satellite images showed a Turkish-made Akinci combat drone at Egypt's East Oweinat airstrip near the Sudan border in Dec 2025.
links.returns: No material return documented. Reuters describes Egypt's interest as a SAF-run state aligned with Cairo on Nile water (GERD) and border security.
links.position: Cairo backs Sudan's state institutions and the army as the legitimate authority.

links.actions: Amended Sicomines deal (2024): Chinese partners to fund up to US$7bn of infrastructure, tied to copper prices.
links.position: Kinshasa says the renegotiation raised its share of benefits.

links.actions: 1,306 loan commitments worth US$182.28bn, 2000-2023 (commitments, not disbursements).
links.returns: Varies by loan. Resource-backed in some cases (not itemised here).
links.position: Beijing frames lending as development finance with no political conditions.

links.actions: Brokered the 27 June 2025 DRC-Rwanda peace agreement and a Regional Economic Integration Framework on critical-mineral supply chains (signed 4 Dec 2025).
links.returns: Framework for US-linked investment in DRC and Rwanda mineral supply chains.
links.position: Washington presents it as peace through economic integration. Critics argue minerals access is the main US aim.

links.actions: France handed over its last base in Chad on 30 January 2025, two months after N'Djamena ended the defence pact.
links.position: Chad says the break is military only, not diplomatic.

links.actions: Cargo flights from Syria to Al-Khadim airbase rose in late 2024. RFI reports the base serves as a hub for Russian arms moving to Mali, Burkina Faso and other Sahel states.
links.returns: A Mediterranean and Sahel logistics hub after Syria.
links.position: Moscow describes its presence as security cooperation at the invitation of Libyan authorities.

links.actions: Sudan's foreign minister said in Feb 2025 the two sides agreed on a 25-year naval logistics point near Port Sudan (up to 4 ships, 300 personnel), pending ratification.
links.position: Khartoum says ratification awaits an elected parliament. The deal is unratified.

links.actions: Niger said in Sept 2025 it wants Rosatom to build two reactors and cooperate on uranium. No construction contract reported.
links.returns: Prospective nuclear and uranium access after Orano's exit.
links.position: Niamey frames it as sovereignty over its uranium.

links.actor: Somali federal government / Puntland vs ISIS-Somalia and al-Shabaab
links.actions: AFRICOM carried out 124 airstrikes in Somalia in 2025, many against ISIS-Somalia in Puntland's Golis Mountains.
links.returns: Counter-terrorism aims. No resource return identified.
links.position: Washington says the strikes protect the US homeland and support Somali forces.

links.actions: US forces left Air Base 201 (Agadez) on 5 Aug 2024 and completed withdrawal from Niger on 15 Sep 2024.
links.returns: n/a (loss of the main US drone base in the Sahel).
links.position: Niamey revoked the military accord, calling it imposed.

links.actions: Niger nationalised SOMAIR in June 2025, removing Orano's 63.4% control. Orano took it to arbitration.
links.returns: Loss of uranium access for Orano (reverse flow).
links.position: Niamey frames it as resource sovereignty. Orano calls it unlawful.

sahel.bottom: Military governments in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger are fighting al-Qa'ida's JNIM and Islamic State's Sahel branch for the countryside, and they have replaced French and UN support with Russian forces while taking tighter state control of gold and uranium. [[reuters-mali-2025,uk-proscribed,reuters-somair-2025]]

paras.t: The three juntas face one insurgency rather than three. {{g-jnim|JNIM}}, a federation of al-Qa'ida-aligned groups formed in March 2017, operates across northern and central Mali, northern Burkina Faso and western Niger. [[uk-proscribed]] Islamic State's Sahel Province, which split from al-Mourabitoun in May 2015, fights mainly in the {{liptako|Liptako-Gourma}} border zone shared by all three states. [[acled-issp-profile]]

Russia filled the security gap France left. {{bamako|Bamako}} kept Russia's Africa Corps when Wagner left in June 2025. [[reuters-mali-2025]] Russian defence-ministry personnel arrived in {{ouaga|Ouagadougou}} in January 2024 to protect Captain Traoré, and instructors with an air-defence system reached {{niamey|Niamey}} in April 2024. [[reuters-bf-ru-2024,reuters-niger-ru-2024]]

Gold pays for the fighting. Armed groups tax and protect artisanal mining sites, which gives them income and local standing. [[gitoc-acled-2024]] Niger's army raided such sites in June 2025 to cut jihadist financing. [[reuters-niger-gold-2025]] Much of the region's gold leaves undeclared: SWISSAID found 405 t of African gold entered the UAE in 2022 without matching export records. [[swissaid-gold-2024]] SWISSAID names Mali among the three largest gold-smuggling countries in Africa and finds that 80-85% of African artisanal gold is exported to the UAE. [[swissaid-gold-2024]]

The juntas treat minerals as a test of sovereignty. Niger moved in June 2025 to nationalise Orano's SOMAIR uranium mine at {{arlit|Arlit}}. [[reuters-somair-2025]] Mali began building a gold refinery with Russia's Yadran Group as a minority partner, which gives Moscow a commercial stake alongside its security role. [[reuters-mali-refinery]]

Each side's case: the juntas say Western forces failed to stop the insurgency and that state control returns mineral revenue to citizens. [[reuters-somair-2025]] Orano says SOMAIR operated under valid agreements and calls the nationalisation unlawful. [[orano-somair-2025]] Algeria, the largest neighbour, approved sending military units to Niger in October 2026. [[lemonde-alg-niger-2026]]

lake-chad.bottom: Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) and Boko Haram are fighting the armies around Lake Chad, and ISWAP has been overrunning isolated army outposts in north-east Nigeria. [[reuters-nigeria-surge-2025,iss-iswap-2025]]

paras.t: {{g-iswap|ISWAP}} grew out of Boko Haram's 2015 pledge of allegiance to Islamic State, according to its UN sanctions entry. [[un-1267]] Reuters reported a surge in attacks in north-east Nigeria in early 2025 that officials described as a jihadist comeback. [[reuters-nigeria-surge-2025]]

The outposts are exposed because of how Nigeria chose to resettle civilians. It set up remote military outposts to resettle displaced people in destroyed towns, and ISS counted at least 15 ISWAP attacks on such outposts in the first half of 2025. [[iss-iswap-2025]] Each overrun base also arms the group, because ISWAP seizes the weapons it finds there. [[iss-iswap-2025]]

The {{lake|lake}} itself shapes the war. It shrank by about 90% between 1963 and 2001, according to FAO, which cut the fishing, farming and grazing that lakeshore communities rely on. [[fao-lakechad]] Its islands and marshes now give ISWAP a base that armies struggle to reach. [[iss-iswap-2025]]

Chad changed security partners. It ended its defence pact with France in November 2024, and France handed over its last base in {{ndj|N'Djamena}} in January 2025. [[ap-chad-2025]] N'Djamena presents the move as restoring full sovereignty over its security choices. [[ap-chad-2025]]

sudan.bottom: Sudan's army (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have fought for control of the state since April 2023, and both depend on gold revenue and on foreign suppliers of drones and arms. [[un-sudan-2024,reuters-sudan-backers-2023]]

paras.t: The war has split the country east and west. The army-led government moved to {{portsudan|Port Sudan}}, while the RSF said it captured the army's headquarters in {{fasher|El Fasher}}, capital of North {{darfur|Darfur}}, in October 2025. [[reuters-ru-sudan-base-2025,reuters-elfasher-2025]]

Gold is the main source of hard currency for both sides, and most of it goes to the UAE. The RSF's business network began in the {{jebelamer|Jebel Amer}} mines of Darfur. [[guardian-jebelamer-2020]] SWISSAID counts 29 t of gold the UAE imported directly from Sudan in 2024, plus imports via Chad and Libya that it treats as exit routes for RSF gold. [[swissaid-uae-2025]] The US Treasury sanctioned UAE-based AZ Gold, managed by an RSF figure, for buying Sudanese gold. [[ofac-rsf-2025]]

Foreign supply keeps both sides fighting. UN experts found credible allegations of UAE arms flights to the RSF through eastern Chad, and the US Treasury sanctioned UAE-based companies that supplied the RSF with money and equipment. [[un-sudan-2024,ofac-rsf-2025]] The army fields Turkish Baykar drones and Iranian drones, and Egypt has deployed drones to its border. [[wapo-baykar-2025,reuters-iran-drones-2024,reuters-egypt-drones-2026]]

Civilians bear the cost. Fighting reached the {{gezira|Gezira}} irrigation scheme, Sudan's main grain area, and cut wheat and sorghum output. [[fao-sudan-ag-2024]] The UN rights office said drone strikes killed 306 people in three weeks in October 2026. [[radiotamazuj-drones-2026]]

Each side's case: the army presents itself as the national army defending the state against a rebel militia, and the RSF says it is fighting remnants of Bashir's Islamist regime. [[reuters-sudan-backers-2023]] The UAE denies arming any party and says its flights carry aid. [[un-sudan-2024]]

great-lakes.bottom: In eastern DR Congo, the M23/AFC rebellion holds much of North and South Kivu with Rwandan troops alongside it, according to UN experts, and the Rubaya coltan mines are one of the main prizes. [[un-drc-2024,un-drc-s2024-969]]

paras.t: UN experts reported 3,000 to 4,000 Rwandan troops fighting with {{g-m23|M23}} in 2024, around {{goma|Goma}} and later {{bukavu|Bukavu}}. [[un-drc-2024]] {{kigali|Kigali}} denies backing the group and says it is defending itself against the FDLR, a militia with roots in the 1994 genocide. [[un-drc-2024]]

Territory turns into revenue through minerals. M23 has held the {{rubaya|Rubaya}} coltan mines since April 2024, and UN experts found coltan from there was exported fraudulently to Rwanda and mixed with Rwandan output. [[un-drc-s2024-969,reuters-drc-rwanda-coltan-2025]] This matters beyond the region because Rubaya is a major source of the world's tantalum. [[un-drc-s2024-969,usgs-tantalum]]

The south's {{katanga|copper-cobalt belt}} ties Congo to China's battery supply chain. China imported 628,191 t of cobalt intermediates from DR Congo in 2024, 98% of its imports by weight. [[wits-cobalt-2024]]

Washington links peace to minerals. It brokered a DR Congo–Rwanda peace agreement in June 2025 and a regional economic framework in December 2025 that ties security to legal mineral trade and investment. [[state-drc-rwanda-2025,state-reif-2025]] Kinshasa calls M23 a Rwandan proxy that loots its minerals. [[un-drc-2025]]

car.bottom: The Central African Republic's government has extended its control with Russian and Rwandan forces, and Russian-linked firms are paid partly in gold, timber and tax breaks. [[icg-car-2026]]

paras.t: President Touadéra won a third term in December 2025, and the constitutional court validated the result. [[reuters-car-court-2026]] About 1,500 Wagner fighters and Rwandan troops back his government, according to Crisis Group. [[icg-car-2026]]

Security is paid for in resources. Crisis Group reports that Russians run gold mines, cut timber and receive tax exemptions in return for protecting the government. [[icg-car-2026]] The US Treasury sanctioned Wagner-linked firms including Midas, which holds the {{ndassima|Ndassima}} gold mine. [[ofac-wagner-gold]] Treasury said Dubai-based Industrial Resources joined a scheme that turned CAR gold into dollars and moved cash to Russia by hand. [[ofac-wagner-gold]]

{{bangui|Bangui}} argues that Russian and Rwandan forces delivered security gains that UN peacekeeping did not. Moscow is pressing for Africa Corps, under its defence ministry, to replace Wagner and for the government to pay more. [[icg-car-2026]]

horn.bottom: The Horn has two fault lines: Ethiopia's disputes with Eritrea and Egypt over sea access and the Nile, and Somalia's war against al-Shabaab and Islamic State, which the US backs with air strikes. [[reuters-eth-eri-2025,reuters-gerd-2025,hiiraan-africom-2026]]

paras.t: Ethiopia's leaders call sea access existential for the landlocked country. Abiy ruled out war in March 2025, but his army chief and an ambassador later spoke of taking back Eritrea's {{assab|Assab}} port. [[reuters-eth-eri-2025,bbc-eth-eri-2025]] Eritrea calls this irredentism, and it signed a security pact with Egypt. [[bbc-eth-eri-2025]]

The Nile adds a second dispute. Ethiopia opened the {{gerd|GERD}} dam in September 2025, and Egypt called it illegal because it relies on the Nile for most of its fresh water. [[reuters-gerd-2025]] Ethiopia calls the dam a development project that harms no one downstream. [[reuters-gerd-2025]]

In Somalia, US Africa Command carried out 124 strikes in 2025, against {{g-issom|Islamic State-Somalia}} in Puntland and {{g-shabaab|al-Shabaab}}. [[hiiraan-africom-2026,africom-isis-somalia-2025]] Al-Shabaab, an al-Qa'ida affiliate, has fought the Somali government since 2007. [[uk-proscribed]]

China's footprint follows the trade route to the sea. It financed and built the railway from {{addis|Addis Ababa}} to {{djibouti|Djibouti}}, and it opened its first overseas {{cn-djib|military base}} there in 2017. [[aiddata-addis-djib,reuters-djib-base-2017]]

coastal-wa.bottom: JNIM's insurgency has reached the northern borderlands of Benin and Togo, and coastal states' gold trade feeds the same UAE-bound flows seen in the Sahel. [[reuters-benin-54-2025,swissaid-uae-2025]]

paras.t: The spillover is now deadly. Benin first reported eight soldiers killed in a JNIM attack in {{nbenin|its northern border parks}} in April 2025, then acknowledged 54 after JNIM claimed 70. [[reuters-benin-54-2025]]

Coastal states are also transit points for gold. The UAE's records show an anomaly: Togo is not a significant gold producer, yet the UAE recorded 52 t imported from it in 2024, a gap SWISSAID highlights in its analysis of conflict gold. [[swissaid-uae-2025]]
Ghana shows the scale of informal mining. Small-scale miners produced 39% of its gold in 2024. [[ecofin-ghana-asm-2025]]

southern.bottom: An Islamic State-linked insurgency in Mozambique's Cabo Delgado province sits beside a $20bn LNG project, and Rwandan troops have been central to protecting it. [[acled-rwanda-moz-2025,reuters-mozlng-2025]]

paras.t: More than 4,000 Rwandan troops fight alongside Mozambique's army in {{cabo|Cabo Delgado}}, funded partly by the EU. [[acled-rwanda-moz-2025,club-moz-rwanda-2025]] The US designated {{g-ism|Islamic State-Mozambique}} a terrorist organisation in 2021. [[state-fto]]
The deployment protects the zone around the {{afungi|Afungi}} gas site. TotalEnergies lifted force majeure on its Mozambique LNG project in October 2025. [[reuters-mozlng-2025]]
ACLED credits Rwanda's forces with pushing back the insurgents but finds limits to civilian protection. [[acled-rwanda-moz-2025]]

north.bottom: Libya remains split between a Tripoli government and Khalifa Haftar's eastern forces, and the east has become a logistics hub for Russian forces in the Sahel. [[rfi-alkhadim-2025,cnn-libya-flights-2024]]

paras.t: Haftar's forces host Russian logistics at {{khadim|al-Khadim}} airbase east of {{benghazi|Benghazi}}. Russian military flights from Syria to eastern Libya rose in late 2024. [[cnn-libya-flights-2024]] RFI reports that al-Khadim serves as a hub for Russian arms moving to Mali, Burkina Faso and other Sahel states. [[rfi-alkhadim-2025]]

Turkey backs the other side. It intervened openly for the {{tripoli|Tripoli}} government in January 2020 with officers, drones, air defences and Syrian fighters, which halted Haftar's offensive on the capital. [[icg-turkey-libya-2020]]
Oil revenue is divided along the same line, with the east-based authorities shutting fields in August 2024. [[eia-libya]]
Libya is also a gold corridor. SWISSAID counts 9 t of gold the UAE imported from Libya in 2024 and treats Libya as one exit route for Sudanese gold. [[swissaid-uae-2025]]
Each side's case: Turkey says its support is legal because Tripoli requested it under a bilateral agreement. The UN considers the arms transfers a breach of its embargo. [[icg-libya-update-2]]

a7.t: Russia's sanctioned A7 payment network and its ruble stablecoin A7A5 are one reported route by which Sahel gold proceeds can reach Russia. No public source traces a specific shipment of African gold through it.
